title: Vector subset sum over F3

problem.name: Average-case $\mathbb F_3^n$-Subset-Sum
problem.statement_latex: Given independent uniform vectors $h_1,\ldots,h_m\in\mathbb F_3^n$, find a nonempty $S\subseteq\{1,\ldots,m\}$ such that $\sum_{i\in S}h_i=0$. The coefficients are restricted to $\{0,1\}$. This is a finite-field subset-sum problem related to restricted short integer solutions. Complexity is measured in quantum gates and classical bit operations on the explicit input.

quantum.details_latex: For every fixed $\kappa>\log_2 3$ and $m\ge\kappa n$, success probability is at least $1-2^{-\Omega_\kappa(m)}$. The algorithm combines quantum filtering with a deterministic binary-error LWE decoder.

classical.headline_latex: $\operatorname{poly}(n,m)2^{O(n/\log(m/n))}$ time in the Wagner regime; polynomial time above the classical vector-count threshold.
classical.headline_text: $\operatorname{poly}(n,m)2^{O(n/\log(m/n))}$ time in the Wagner regime; polynomial time above the classical vector-count threshold.
classical.details_latex: For $m/n\to\infty$ below the known polynomial-time thresholds, Wagner-type algorithms merge lists of partial sums while imposing zero coordinates. For bounded $m/n$, known algorithms have $2^{O(n)}$ time. Kothari--O'Donnell--Wu give a deterministic polynomial-time algorithm, valid even for worst-case inputs, when $m\ge n^2/3+Cn\log n$ for an absolute constant $C$. Kothari--Metger--O'Donnell--Shutty--Wu further announce a polynomial-time threshold $m\ge c_\star n^2$, where $c_\star=(8\log_2 3-9)/36\approx0.1022$; Section 1.3 presents this as an announced construction with its formal proof deferred. The classical comparison takes the fastest applicable algorithm at the given $n,m$.

strength.description_latex: Subexponential to polynomial in the strongest comparison. The quantum tradeoff reaches polynomial time throughout $m=\Omega(n^2)$, extending below the smallest reported classical polynomial-time vector-count threshold. The general bounds also describe intermediate improvements when both algorithms have superpolynomial time; their degree depends on the input density $m/n$.

evidence.description_latex: Partial evidence from the classical frontier; the quantum running-time theorem is rigorous. The tradeoff is a September 2026 preprint.

hardware.description_latex: The Fourier construction has $m+n$ qutrit registers, together with the workspace for a reversible decoder. The gate count and decoder workspace follow the parameter-dependent running time. The polynomial-time regime has polynomial logical resources; larger decoding costs require correspondingly longer fault-tolerant computations.
